Where rental yields are highest in Catalonia, Valencia and the Balearic Islands

Gross apartment yields for 127 comarcas, towns, islands and areas of eastern Spain, with the income and population around every provincial capital and a look at tenanted investments on the market.

By Casafari ResearchPublished 17 October 2026Data: October 2025 – September 2026
Passeig de Gràcia, Barcelona · photo: Txllxt TxllxT, CC BY-SA 4.0

The short answer

Yields rise as prices fall. Inland comarcas of Catalonia and Valencia pay 8–11% gross; the big coastal cities pay about 6%; the Balearic Islands pay 3.6–5.2%.

6.4%Barcelona (Barcelonès): €25/m² rent on €4,722/m². Catalonia’s median comarca yields 6.2%, led by Ribera d'Ebre at 11.0%.
6.0%València city: €17/m² rent on €3,381/m². The Valencian median is 7.2%, led by Canal de Navarrés at 11.2%.
4.5%Palma: €20/m² rent on €5,375/m². Mallorca yields 4.4% overall; inland Sa Pobla reaches 7.5%.
How yield is measuredAll three regionsCataloniaValencian CommunityBalearic IslandsFAQMethodology

What gross rental yield means here

Gross rental yield is one year of rent divided by the purchase price. This report uses average asking rents and asking prices for apartments per square metre over the twelve months to September 2026: rent per m² × 12 ÷ price per m². An area where flats ask €12/m² a month and €2,000/m² to buy yields 7.2%. Gross yield ignores costs, vacancies and taxes, so it is best used to compare places, not to value a single flat.

All three regions

Yields fall as prices rise, everywhere on the coast

Region 1

Rental yields in Catalonia

45 comarcas across Barcelona, Girona, Tarragona and Lleida.

The highest rental yields in Catalonia are inland. Ribera d'Ebre returns about 11.0% gross, and Priorat, Àrea de Balaguer and Alt Camp pay 8.4–8.6%. Barcelonès, which includes Barcelona city, yields 6.4% on the region’s highest prices; the Costa Brava comarcas of Baix and Alt Empordà pay about 7%.

The median comarca yields 6.2%. The spread is driven by price, not rent: Barcelonès asks about five and a half times what Ribera d’Ebre asks per square metre, but rents for only about three times as much.

Region 2

Rental yields in the Valencian Community

26 comarcas of Valencia and Alicante and 18 towns of Castellón.

The best rental yields in the Valencian Community are in inland Valencia province. Canal de Navarrés pays about 11.2% and Vall d'Aiora 10.1%. On the coast, Xilxes (9.5%) and Moncofa (8.3%) in Castellón beat the big cities.

València city yields 6.0%. In Alicante, the L’Alacantí comarca yields 5.9% and the Benidorm coast of Marina Baixa 5.4%: tourism lifts prices faster than long-term rents. The regional median is 7.2%.

Region 3

Rental yields in the Balearic Islands

Four islands and 34 areas of Mallorca.

The Balearic Islands have the lowest rental yields of the three regions. Ibiza yields 5.2%, Mallorca 4.4%, Menorca 4.0% and Formentera 3.6%. Prices are the highest in this report: €7,151/m² in Ibiza and €8,267/m² in Formentera.

Inside Mallorca, inland towns pay most. Sa Pobla yields 7.5% and Mancor de la Vall 6.4%, against 4.5% in Palma and 3.0% in Andratx, the island’s most expensive area.

Frequently asked questions

Where are rental yields highest in Catalonia?

Inland comarcas in Tarragona and Lleida lead. Ribera d'Ebre returns about 11.0% gross, and Priorat, Àrea de Balaguer and Alt Camp sit between 8.4% and 8.6%. The median across Catalonia's comarcas is 6.2%.

What is the gross rental yield in Barcelona?

Apartments in the Barcelonès comarca, which includes Barcelona city, ask about €25/m² a month to rent and €4,722/m² to buy, a gross yield of about 6.4%.

What is the rental yield in Valencia city?

In València city apartments ask about €17/m² a month and €3,381/m² to buy, a gross yield of about 6.0%.

Where are the best rental yields in the Valencian Community?

Inland Valencia province leads: Canal de Navarrés at about 11.2% and Vall d'Aiora at 10.1%. On the coast, Xilxes (9.5%) and Moncofa (8.3%) in Castellón stand out.

What are rental yields in the Balearic Islands?

The lowest of the three regions. By island: Ibiza 5.2%, Mallorca 4.4%, Menorca 4.0% and Formentera 3.6%. Inland Mallorca does better, led by Sa Pobla at 7.5%.

What is the rental yield in Palma de Mallorca?

About 4.5% gross: apartments ask €20/m² a month to rent and €5,375/m² to buy.

How is gross rental yield calculated?

Gross rental yield is a year of rent divided by the purchase price. With asking figures per square metre: monthly rent per m² × 12 ÷ price per m². For example, €12/m² × 12 ÷ €2,000/m² = 7.2%. It ignores costs, vacancy and taxes.

Which provincial capital has the largest catchment and the highest incomes?

València: 623,985 people live within a 10-minute drive of its centre. Around the centres of Barcelona and València, 67% of households earn more than €40,000 a year, followed by Palma at 66%.

Methodology

Prices and rents. Average asking price and asking rent per square metre for apartments, October 2025 to September 2026, from Casafari Area Insights, with extreme prices left out. Areas are the comarcas of Catalonia, Valencia and Alicante, the main towns of Castellón, the four Balearic islands and the areas of Mallorca.

Gross yield. Rent per m² × 12 ÷ price per m². Rents are reported in whole euros per square metre, so yields in the cheapest areas carry about half a point of rounding. Two very small rental markets are shown in the tables but left out of rankings and headline answers.

Income and population. Casafari Claro AI Location Intelligence at each provincial capital’s centre: residents within a 10-minute walk and drive, household income bands, spending power and footfall.

Investment properties. Casafari Claro AI searches of retail premises for sale described as let to a tenant, run on 17 October 2026. Details are available through the Casafari MCP.
